items.title: Depth with respect to an ideal
items.strategy: For a finite module define I-depth as the supremum of lengths of M-regular sequences in I, fixing the IM=M and zero-module values as infinity; local depth uses the maximal ideal.

items.title: Depth is infinite when the ideal acts surjectively
items.strategy: Unpack the infinity convention for IM=M, then use Nakayama to exclude this case for a finite nonzero local module and a proper ideal in its maximal ideal.

items.title: A regular element exists by prime avoidance
items.strategy: For IM != M, identify zero divisors on a nonzero finite module through associated primes, use their finiteness and finite prime avoidance to choose an element of I outside their union, and check its quotient remains nonzero.

items.title: Depth zero and associated primes
items.strategy: Translate depth zero into absence of an M-regular element in I and apply the prime-avoidance lemma in both directions.

items.title: The local depth-zero associated-prime criterion
items.strategy: Specialize the ideal criterion to the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring, retaining finite and nonzero-module hypotheses.

items.title: A maximal regular sequence stops at an associated prime
items.strategy: Apply the depth-zero associated-prime criterion to the terminal quotient, obtaining both the obstruction to extension and its converse.

items.title: Ext degree zero identifies ideal-annihilated elements
items.strategy: Evaluate Hom_R(R/I,M) at one modulo I to identify it with (0:_M I), making nonvanishing the degree-zero obstruction.

items.title: The first nonzero Ext shifts across a regular element
items.strategy: Apply Ext_R(R/I,-) to 0 to M to M to M/xM to 0; x in I acts as zero on Ext, so exactness gives the shift through the first nonzero degree.

items.title: Maximal regular sequences have a common Ext length
items.strategy: Iterate the Ext shift to a terminal depth-zero quotient, making each maximal length equal to the same first nonzero Ext degree.

items.title: Depth as the first nonzero Ext degree
items.strategy: Compare the regular-sequence definition with the common Ext length, retaining the infinity case when every relevant Ext group vanishes.

items.title: Depth equals the maximal regular-sequence length
items.strategy: Package the comparison for finite modules over a Noetherian ring and state the common-length maximal-sequence conclusion in the local/Jacobson setting.

items.title: Radical invariance of first nonzero Ext
items.strategy: Use powers witnessing equal radicals and finite quotient filtrations to compare the Ext-vanishing ranges for I and J.

items.title: Depth depends only on the radical of the ideal
items.strategy: Translate the equality of first nonzero Ext degrees for equal radicals back into equality of depths.

items.title: Depth drops by one after quotienting by a regular element
items.strategy: Use the regular-element Ext shift, including the convention boundary cases, to prove depth_I(M/xM)=depth_I(M)-1.

items.title: A prime minimal over an associated prime plus one element becomes associated after a power quotient
items.strategy: Embed N = R/p in M, apply Artin--Rees to choose n with N intersect x^nM contained in xN, and use the induced injection of N/(N intersect x^nM) into M/x^nM together with its quotient onto R/(p+(x)) to make every prime minimal over p+(x) minimal in the relevant support and hence associated to M/x^nM.

items.title: Depth is bounded by the quotient dimension at every associated prime
items.strategy: Follow Stacks Lemma 10.72.9: induct on depth, choose a regular x, choose q minimal over p+(x) with dim(R/q)=dim(R/p)-1, use the power-quotient associated-prime lemma, and apply the regular-power depth drop to M/x^nM, including the depth-zero and depth-one base cases.

items.title: Localization gives the stated depth inequality
items.strategy: For a prime p prove depth(M_p)+dim(R/p) >= depth(M) as in Stacks Lemma 10.72.10. If the inequality is not immediate, the associated-prime quotient-dimension bound and finite prime avoidance produce an M-regular element x in p; quotient by x and induct on depth, treating M_p=0 with the infinity convention.

items.title: Radical, localization, and regular-quotient properties of depth
items.strategy: State the source-qualified radical, localization, and one-step quotient results as a synthesis of the focused preceding results rather than a duplicate proof package.

items.title: The middle lower bound in the Depth Lemma
items.strategy: Read the Ext vanishing range for the middle term from the long exact Ext sequence of a short exact sequence.

items.title: The left lower bound in the Depth Lemma
items.strategy: Inspect adjacent Ext terms to convert their vanishing range into the lower bound for the left term.

items.title: The right lower bound in the Depth Lemma
items.strategy: Use the remaining adjacent Ext terms to derive the lower bound for the quotient term, with its one-degree shift explicit.

items.title: The three Depth Lemma inequalities
items.strategy: Assemble the three focused Ext-vanishing inequalities for a short exact sequence, preserving term order and plus/minus-one shifts.

items.title: Unequal-depth equalities in a short exact sequence
items.strategy: Combine pairs of Depth Lemma inequalities in the standard strict-depth ranges and identify the third depth only after checking the minimum is strict.

items.title: Depth from first nonzero Koszul cohomology
items.strategy: Use finite dimension from the height theorem, induction on depth, the finite associated-prime/prime-avoidance depth-zero case, regular-element shifts, and finite-free Koszul self-duality to identify first cohomology and complementary last homology with depth.

items.title: Depth is bounded by the number of ideal generators
items.strategy: The n-generator Koszul complex has no degrees beyond n, and M/IM nonzero excludes the infinity convention.

items.title: The Koszul characterization of depth
items.strategy: State the first-nonzero-cohomology and last-nonzero-homology formulations with their source convention and finiteness hypotheses.

items.title: Depth at a prime is bounded by local support dimension
items.strategy: Each regular element gives a strict support-dimension descent via the principal ideal theorem; compare sequence length with local support dimension.

items.title: A finite local module has depth at most its dimension
items.strategy: Specialize the local-prime bound at the maximal ideal using the support-dimension convention.

items.title: Depth is bounded by support dimension
items.strategy: Record the finite nonzero local-module inequality in support-dimension form, separating its zero-module convention.

items.title: Cohen--Macaulay local modules and rings
items.strategy: Define a nonzero finite local module to be Cohen--Macaulay exactly when local depth equals support dimension, and a local ring by applying this to itself.

items.title: Maximal and global Cohen--Macaulay modules
items.strategy: Define maximal Cohen--Macaulay by equality with the ring dimension and global Cohen--Macaulayness by localization at every support prime; record the zero-module convention.

items.title: Zero-dimensional finite local modules are Cohen--Macaulay
items.strategy: The depth upper bound and nonnegative regular-sequence definition force both invariants to equal zero.

items.title: A regular parameter quotient preserves the depth--dimension gap
items.strategy: Combine the one-step depth quotient formula with exact parameter dimension drop, retaining the parameter and nonzerodivisor hypotheses.

items.title: Cohen--Macaulayness and a regular parameter quotient
items.strategy: Subtract one from both invariants in the gap lemma to prove the two-way equivalence under its stated hypotheses.

items.title: Regular quotients and Cohen--Macaulayness
items.strategy: Iterate the one-step equivalence along a regular parameter sequence, retaining properness and finite-module qualifications.

items.title: Associated primes of a Cohen--Macaulay module have full dimension
items.strategy: For p in Ass(M), apply the associated-prime depth bound depth(M) <= dim(R/p); combine Cohen--Macaulay equality depth(M)=dim Supp(M) with the reverse inequality dim(R/p) <= dim Supp(M).

items.title: Cohen--Macaulay modules have no embedded associated primes
items.strategy: Use the full-dimension equality to rule out strict containment above a smaller support prime.

items.title: Associated primes of Cohen--Macaulay modules
items.strategy: Package the full quotient-dimension conclusion, minimality in support, and absence of embedded associated primes.

items.title: The first parameter of a Cohen--Macaulay module is regular
items.strategy: A first parameter avoids all associated primes of full dimension, so the associated-prime criterion makes it a nonzerodivisor.

items.title: Induction along a Cohen--Macaulay parameter sequence
items.strategy: After the first parameter is regular, use the regular-quotient equivalence and parameter dimension drop to identify the remaining tuple as a parameter system on the quotient.

items.title: Every system of parameters is regular in a Cohen--Macaulay module
items.strategy: Apply the parameter induction to the full system and retain the terminal nonzero quotient condition.

items.title: One regular system of parameters implies Cohen--Macaulayness
items.strategy: A regular system has length equal to support dimension, furnishing a depth lower bound matching the general upper bound.

items.title: Parameters and regular sequences in Cohen--Macaulay modules
items.strategy: State both directions: every parameter system in a nonzero finite Cohen--Macaulay local module is regular, and a regular parameter system forces Cohen--Macaulayness.

items.title: Localization preserves the Cohen--Macaulay depth--dimension equality
items.strategy: Follow Stacks Lemma 10.103.11. Induct along a maximal prime chain from p to the local maximal ideal, reduce to a saturated one-step inclusion, combine depth(M_p)+dim(R/p) >= depth(M) with the one-step support-dimension drop, and close with the general depth upper bound; treat M_p=0 separately.

items.title: Cohen--Macaulayness localizes
items.strategy: Apply the localized equality at every support prime and then invoke the global Cohen--Macaulay convention.

items.title: Localization of Cohen--Macaulay modules
items.strategy: State the finite Noetherian localization theorem in local and global forms, distinguishing support primes from zero localizations.

items.title: A polynomial variable increases depth by one
items.strategy: Prove coefficientwise that x is regular on M[x], identify its quotient by x with M, and apply the one-step depth formula after localization.

items.title: Polynomial extension preserves Cohen--Macaulayness
items.strategy: At a polynomial prime compare the one-variable depth and support-dimension increments, then iterate variables.

items.title: Polynomial extensions of Cohen--Macaulay rings
items.strategy: Specialize the module result to the ring module and state the global localization convention for finitely many variables.

items.title: Completion preserves regular sequences
items.strategy: Use flat completion to preserve injections and faithful flatness to preserve nonzero terminal quotients for finite modules.

items.title: Completion reflects depth
items.strategy: Use flat base change for Ext from the residue field and faithful flatness to preserve the first nonzero Ext degree, including the infinity case.

items.title: Completion preserves Cohen--Macaulayness in both directions
items.strategy: Use equality of depths from reflection and equality of support dimensions under completion to prove the local-ring and finite-module equivalence.

items.title: Completion preserves Cohen--Macaulayness
items.strategy: Package the two-way completion theorem with its Noetherian local, finite-module, and completion-ideal hypotheses.

items.title: A flat local map splits regular sequences into base and fibre parts
items.strategy: For a flat local map, base-change a regular sequence from the source and then lift a regular closed-fibre sequence, verifying regularity one quotient at a time.

items.title: Depth is additive for a flat local homomorphism
items.strategy: The split sequence gives one bound; the Ext/Koszul vanishing characterization gives the reverse under the exact Noetherian and closed-fibre hypotheses.

items.title: The flat-local Cohen--Macaulay fibre criterion
items.strategy: Under the source-stated dimension-formula hypotheses, compare additive depth and dimension formulas to obtain the iff criterion for base, fibre, and target.

items.title: The depth formula for flat local homomorphisms
items.strategy: State depth additivity and the Cohen--Macaulay consequence separately for a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings and its closed fibre; do not add a finite-type hypothesis absent from Stacks Lemmas 10.163.2--10.163.3.

title: Depth and Cohen Macaulay Modules — Examples

items.title: A zero-dimensional local ring is Cohen--Macaulay
items.strategy: For a nonzero zero-dimensional Noetherian local ring calculate that support dimension and depth are both zero, then apply the definition.

items.title: Polynomial rings are Cohen--Macaulay
items.strategy: Start from a field and iterate the polynomial-extension theorem, displaying the local regular sequence given by the variables.

items.title: A non-Cohen--Macaulay local quotient
items.strategy: Compute a standard non-equidimensional local quotient's support dimension and use an associated-prime obstruction to force a smaller depth.

items.title: A Cohen--Macaulay ring with zero divisors
items.strategy: Use a hypersurface quotient by a nonzerodivisor to verify Cohen--Macaulayness while displaying nonzero zero divisors, separating the condition from being a domain or reduced.

items.title: A nonfree maximal Cohen--Macaulay module
items.strategy: Present a standard module over a singular hypersurface, compute its depth from a regular sequence, compare it with ring dimension, and separately show it is not free.

items.title: Depth of a hypersurface quotient
items.strategy: Start with a regular local ring and a nonzero regular element, verify regularity, and calculate the one-step depth drop.

items.title: Depth of a union of planes
items.strategy: Use the coordinate-ring short exact sequence for a union of planes, calculate the other depths, and invoke the correctly oriented Depth Lemma inequality.

items.title: The zero-module and surjective-ideal depth conventions
items.strategy: Evaluate the regular-sequence and Ext formulations for the zero module and for IM=M, checking every infinity against the adopted convention.

items.title: Three sharp Depth Lemma inequalities
items.strategy: Work through three short exact sequences chosen so that each Depth Lemma lower bound is attained, tracking the term that realizes its minimum.

items.title: A parameter sequence regular in a hypersurface
items.strategy: Choose a full parameter system in a hypersurface local ring and verify successive nonzerodivisors by the Cohen--Macaulay parameter theorem.

items.title: A parameter sequence that fails in a non-Cohen--Macaulay ring
items.strategy: In a reducible local quotient choose a parameter in an associated prime, prove it is a zero divisor, and calculate the depth gap.

items.title: Associated primes are unmixed in a Cohen--Macaulay example
items.strategy: Compute associated primes of a Cohen--Macaulay hypersurface with zero divisors and verify that every quotient has the full dimension required by the theorem.

items.title: A depth computation before and after completion
items.strategy: Use the same finite regular sequence in a small local quotient and its completion, calculate depth on both sides, and identify faithful flatness preserving the conclusion.
